transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-15
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood PE), Aisha (Nova Head of AI), Mark (Platform), Simon (CTO), Priya (Security)
Links shared: redwood/pilots/novaretail-deck.pdf, redwood/benchmarks/novaretail-harness.csv

-- Auto summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete) --
- Goal: scope pilot success criteria (latency, quality, cost), decide initial deployment posture (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and define benchmark plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can do quick intros, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, Sofia's our SE, Evan's on perf.
[00:12] Aisha: Hi, Aisha here. Big thanks, excited to scope this out, we've been digging into options to reduce latency at peak and also lock down PII rules.
[00:22] Mark: Mark from platform, we're mainly worried about throughput and the knee in cost when traffic peaks.
[00:30] Sofia: Great, quick agenda: success criteria, current workload shape and metrics, a benchmark plan, and then recommended deployment pathways.
[00:40] Simon: Sounds good. Quick callout, we have a compliance window, can't push anything that touches raw PII into a public SaaS without DPA addendum, so private or VPC is likely.
[00:54] Jordan: Noted. We'll walk through the tradeoffs.
[01:05] Sofia: Can we start with success criteria — Aisha, what does success look like for this pilot?
[01:12] Aisha: Two things: 1) sub-200ms 95th percentile for single-shot personalization queries during 500rps peak, 2) no PII persisted in logs and ability to run on-prem if needed. Also a quality bar — CTR on recommendations must improve by >6% in A/B.
[01:36] Evan: Quick clarification, 500 requests per second is sustained or burst?
[01:40] Mark: That'd be a sustained peak for holiday windows, bursts up to 800rps for 30s windows.
[01:47] Sofia: Ok, that's helpful. That workload profile pushes towards dedicated GPU pools for predictable tail-latency; hosted can do it but cost and SLOs vary.
[02:00] Priya: On the PII point — we have customer names, order numbers, partial addresses. Our legal team prefers not to send that to a multi-tenant hosted service unless it's redacted or encrypted. What options do you support?
[02:14] Jordan: We have three deployment modes: Hosted (fastest onboarding, multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, customer-isolated), and Private (VPC or on-prem for full control). For PII, Dedicated with strict log scrubbing or Private with customer KMS is common.
[02:32] Simon: When you say Private on-prem, do you offer a package that runs with our HSM/KMS?
[02:38] Evan: Yes, our Private deployment supports KMS integrations and can be air-gapped; however, there is a setup lead time and an enterprise license.
[02:46] Aisha: Lead time estimate?
[02:48] Jordan: For Private on-prem, plan 8-12 weeks for delivery including security review; Dedicated VPC is typically 3-6 weeks. Hosted is immediate.
[02:58] Mark: Cost delta? If we go Dedicated, what's the uplift vs Hosted?
[03:02] Jordan: It depends on committed capacity and burst model; rough rule -- Dedicated has higher committed OPEX but lower per-token variable cost at scale. We'll send a model spreadsheet.
[03:12] Sofia: Also quantization and batching shift unit cost; for example running a quantized 8-bit model in a dedicated pool with batching reduces per-token by ~30% vs naive hosted inference for this workload pattern — subject to eval.
[03:26] Simon: On batching — what's impact on latency? We need sub-200ms 95p.
[03:31] Evan: Continuous batching helps throughput without hurting tail-latency if you size the pool right; but at very low QPS you'd want single-request paths. In dedicated you can carve out low-latency nodes.
[03:44] (crosstalk)
[03:45] Aisha: Is there a middle ground, like private control plane with hosted compute?
[03:48] Sofia: We do a hybrid where control plane is VPC and compute can be in Redwood-managed clusters in a chosen region — helps with compliance and reduces some setup time.
[03:58] Priya: Ok, about logs — can you redact at the edge and not persist raw inputs?
[04:04] Jordan: Yes. We support prefix/KV cache controls and configurable redaction at the ingress. We can also ship a transform function or provide a filtering lambda before data leaves your network.
[04:16] Priya: Great. Please include that in security docs.
[04:20] Sofia: We'll attach the security checklist (SOC2 cert, ISO, SAML/SSO details, audit log format).
[04:28] Mark: For the benchmark, what should we run?
[04:31] Sofia: We'll propose a harness: steady-state traffic at 500rps, 30s 800rps bursts, sample prompt set of 10k queries representing personalization and search re-rank. We'll measure latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1000-queries.
[04:50] Evan: We'll also test KV cache hit patterns — your prefix caching for product descriptions should reduce compute. Bring a sample of your prompt distribution.
[04:58] Aisha: We'll share the distribution. Any constraints on model size? Our models are 13B tuned variants.
[05:05] Sofia: Good. We'll recommend a 13B or 7B variant depending on perf/quality tradeoffs; quantization effects will be included.
[05:12] Simon: Performance tuning — can you support custom kernels or runtime flags?
[05:16] Evan: We select kernels per architecture, and our runtime exposes a handful of flags for KV cache sizing, prefetch windows, and attention kernels. For bespoke needs we can collaborate with your infra team.
[05:29] (pause)
[05:34] Aisha: Timeline for pilot itself? Ideally we want measurable results before Q1 planning.
[05:39] Jordan: Recommend a 90-day pilot: 2-week lab benchmark -> 30-day pilot with canary traffic -> 60-day ramp + evaluation. That gets you data well before Feb planning.
[05:51] Mark: Who signs the SOW? What's the minimum commitment?
[05:55] Jordan: For Dedicated, standard pilot SOW has a small reserved commit to guarantee capacity; for Hosted you'd do a consumption-based pilot. We'll draft options.
[06:06] Priya: Can you support SOC2 plus our vendor questionnaire?
[06:10] Sofia: Yes, we'll fill the questionnaire and provide the SOC2 report and architecture diagrams.
[06:16] Simon: If we end up on Dedicated but want eventual on-prem, how painful is migration?
[06:22] Evan: We design rollouts to be portable — model versions, prompts, and KV caches can be exported. Private on-prem requires infra parity, but it's planned at the start to avoid rework.
[06:32] Aisha: Any gotchas on GPU types? We have a preference for A100s in our datacenter.
[06:37] Sofia: A100 is supported; for cost-performance we may recommend H100 for next-gen perf but it depends on model and quantization. We'll include a hardware recommendation table.
[06:48] (brief side conversation about holidays schedule)
[07:05] Jordan: Ok quick recap: we have target success criteria (sub-200ms 95p at 500rps with bursts), security constraints leaning private/VPC, agreed benchmark plan and dates. Next steps: Redwood sends cost model, benchmark harness, and security docs; Nova shares PII/PII-redaction rules and sample prompt distribution.
[07:28] Mark: That aligns. We'll aim to get the sample data to you by Friday.
[07:33] Aisha: One more thing — can you run a short A/B with our baseline ranking to validate quality target?
[07:38] Sofia: Yes, we'll include quality evals in the bench plan and capture CTR delta and NDCG.
[07:44] Jordan: Any outstanding blockers?
[07:46] Priya: We need to see the security checklist and confirm KMS integration, otherwise legal won't greenlight hosted.
[07:52] Jordan: We'll prioritize that.
[07:55] (wrap)
[08:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed SOW.

-- End transcript --

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps, occasional mis-heard acronyms ("Samuel" vs SAML), and some proper nouns may be imperfect.
